scenario: Gamma 后端面试，面试官问：「What was a key tradeoff in that project?」你已有大方向但要一秒组织，别像上次「let me, let me think how to say」卡住。
scenario_en: In a Gamma backend interview the interviewer asks, "What was a key tradeoff in that project?" You have the gist but need a beat to organize — not another "let me, let me think how to say" stall.
q: 有初步判断、需要一秒确认取舍，第一句怎么起手？
q_en: You have an instinct but need a beat to check the tradeoff — what's your first line?
options: My first instinct is simplicity over flexibility — let me walk through that tradeoff.
One tradeoff was, um, keeping it simple and make it flexible, so, sorry, let me, let me think how to say...
Oh there were so many tradeoffs on that project — speed, safety, complexity — so many angles I could take, let me figure out which to even talk about first...
There existed a notable tradeoff. I shall now elaborate upon the considerations therein.
tradeoff: 先定方向再想 vs 边复读边卡：给出初步判断买来组织空间，代价是要为方向负责；复读题目省事，却把空白暴露给对方。
why: 有初步判断时先用「My first instinct is X」给方向，再补一句检验取舍，把停顿变成有掌控的思考，而不是把犹豫念出声。
why_en: Lead with "my first instinct is X, then let me check the tradeoff" — it names a direction and turns the pause into visible thinking.
whenOtherWins: 只有当取舍你早想透、能一句说完时，才不用「first instinct」句式，直接给结论更利落。
options_en: My first instinct is simplicity over flexibility — let me walk through that tradeoff.
One tradeoff was, um, keeping it simple and make it flexible, so, sorry, let me, let me think how to say...
Oh there were so many tradeoffs on that project — speed, safety, complexity — so many angles I could take, let me figure out which to even talk about first...
There existed a notable tradeoff. I shall now elaborate upon the considerations therein.
optionMeanings: 先亮出方向判断，再顺势展开取舍。
复读「tradeoff was, um」再「let me think how to say」卡住。
罗列一堆取舍角度，迟迟不选一个讲。
用「I shall elaborate」的书面公文腔开场。
optionMeanings_en: Leads with 'my first instinct is X,' then unpacks the tradeoff.
Repeats 'tradeoff was, um' then stalls on 'let me think how to say.'
Lists many tradeoff angles, never picking one to tell.
Opens in a stiff written 'I shall elaborate' register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方听到明确方向，愿意跟着你的取舍走。
停顿被念出声，显得没组织好。
铺垫太长，对方还没听到任何取舍结论。
像背稿，不像在对话。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They hear a clear direction and follow your tradeoff.
The pause is spoken aloud — reads as unorganized.
Long wind-up; no actual tradeoff lands yet.
Sounds scripted, not like a conversation.
optionDirectness: 抓住「先定方向、再验取舍」的起手节奏。
错在复读加卡壳，把空白念出声。
错在罗列不收口，迟迟不落到一个取舍。
错在语域，口语场合用书面体僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Nails the rhythm: name a direction, then check the tradeoff.
Wrong — echo plus stall, a spoken blank.
Wrong — lists without committing to one tradeoff.
Wrong register — written style is stiff out loud.

scenario: Alterion 技术面，面试官问：「How would you set up the database here?」你上次开口就把 read path 说成「read pass」还卡住。
scenario_en: In an Alterion technical round the interviewer asks, "How would you set up the database here?" Last time you opened by saying "read pass" for read path and stalled.
q: 有好几种做法、想边说边理清，怎么起手最稳？
q_en: There are several options and you want to think aloud — how do you open cleanly?
options: So for the database, I think I would separate the read pass and the write pass, so, so if we want consistency...
There are a couple of ways here — let me start with the simplest and split reads from writes.
Oh databases — SQL, NoSQL, sharding, replication, caching — it depends on so many things, let me think about where to even begin here...
I shall enumerate the available database architectures and evaluate each in turn.
tradeoff: 结构化起手 vs 直接跳进细节卡壳：先说「有几种做法、从最简单的开始」给了框架，代价是多一句；直接跳进去容易词形出错又卡。
why: 读写路径的正确说法是「read path / write path」，不是「read pass」；开口先给「几种做法，从简到繁」的框架再展开。
why_en: It's "read path" and "write path," not "read pass" — open with "a couple of ways, let me start with the simplest," then build.
whenOtherWins: 只有当方案唯一、没有可比选项时，才不用「a couple of ways」框架，直接说那一个即可。
options_en: So for the database, I think I would separate the read pass and the write pass, so, so if we want consistency...
There are a couple of ways here — let me start with the simplest and split reads from writes.
Oh databases — SQL, NoSQL, sharding, replication, caching — it depends on so many things, let me think about where to even begin here...
I shall enumerate the available database architectures and evaluate each in turn.
optionMeanings: 把「read path」说成「read pass」，边说边卡在 consistency。
先说「有几种做法、从最简单的开始」，再分读写。
一口气堆 SQL/NoSQL/分片等名词，不落到方案。
用「I shall enumerate」的书面腔罗列架构。
optionMeanings_en: Says 'read pass' for 'read path,' then stalls on consistency.
Opens 'a couple of ways, start simplest,' then splits reads/writes.
Piles up SQL/NoSQL/sharding names, lands on no plan.
Enumerates architectures in a stiff 'I shall' register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 词形出错又卡壳，显得基础不稳。
给出结构，对方跟着你从简到繁走。
名词轰炸，对方等不到一个具体方案。
像念教科书，聊不下去。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Wrong word form plus a stall — looks shaky on basics.
Gives structure; they follow you from simple upward.
Noun dump; no concrete plan for them to grab.
Reads like a textbook — hard to continue.
optionDirectness: 错在词形（read pass→read path）加卡壳。
抓住「几种做法、从最简单起」的框架起手。
错在罗列名词，没有推进到方案。
错在语域，口语用书面体僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — word form (read pass vs read path) plus a stall.
Nails the frame: a couple of ways, start with the simplest.
Wrong — noun list, no progress to a plan.
Wrong register — bureaucratese is stiff aloud.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读路径：一个查询请求读数据时经过的组件链路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The read path is the chain of components a request goes through when data is read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写路径：一次写入/提交经过的组件链路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The write path is the chain of components a request goes through when data is written.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片：把一份大数据按 key 拆到多台机器上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits one large dataset across multiple machines by a key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复制：把同一份数据在多个副本上保存以提高可用性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replication keeps copies of the same data on multiple replicas for availability.

scenario: Convoke coding 轮，面试官让你「implement a dictionary without using a dictionary」。你有初步思路，别像上次「my initial idea is maybe」绕圈。
scenario_en: In a Convoke coding round you're asked to "implement a dictionary without using a dictionary." You have an idea — don't circle on "my initial idea is maybe" like last time.
q: 有初步思路、想边说边确认可行，怎么起手？
q_en: You have an approach in mind and want to check it aloud — how do you open?
options: My first instinct is an array plus a hash function — let me check that gives O(1) reads.
Oh, so first thing is that the dictionary can read a key one time, so how can I, if I want to read it, my initial idea is maybe...
There's a bunch of ways — hash sets, linked lists, arrays, trees — I could go so many directions, let me just think out loud for a while...
I shall propose a data structure and subsequently verify its asymptotic complexity.
tradeoff: 亮方案再验证 vs 边绕边找：先给一个候选再检验，代价是可能要收回；反复「maybe」听着像还没方向。
why: coding 起手先用「My first instinct is X」亮一个候选方案，再当场验证复杂度，比反复「maybe」绕圈显得有掌控。
why_en: Open coding with "my first instinct is X, let me sanity-check it" — one clear candidate beats circling with "my initial idea is maybe."
whenOtherWins: 只有当题目一眼看不出方向、确实需要先枚举时，才先摆几种再选，而不是硬报一个。
options_en: My first instinct is an array plus a hash function — let me check that gives O(1) reads.
Oh, so first thing is that the dictionary can read a key one time, so how can I, if I want to read it, my initial idea is maybe...
There's a bunch of ways — hash sets, linked lists, arrays, trees — I could go so many directions, let me just think out loud for a while...
I shall propose a data structure and subsequently verify its asymptotic complexity.
optionMeanings: 先报一个候选（数组+哈希函数），再验 O(1)。
自问自答「my initial idea is maybe」绕圈没落点。
罗列一堆结构，说要「想很久」却不选。
用「I shall verify asymptotic complexity」的书面腔。
optionMeanings_en: Names one candidate (array + hash), then checks it's O(1).
Self-talks 'my initial idea is maybe,' circling without landing.
Lists structures, says 'think a while,' never picks.
Stiff 'I shall verify asymptotic complexity' register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官看到你有方案且会自检。
听着像还没方向，浪费开口的机会。
铺垫冗长，迟迟不动手。
像背稿，coding 场合显得僵。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They see you have a plan and self-check it.
Sounds directionless — wastes the opening.
Long wind-up, no actual start.
Scripted — stiff for a coding round.
optionDirectness: 抓住「亮一个候选、再自检 O(1)」的起手。
错在自问自答绕圈，没有推进。
错在罗列不选，迟迟不动手。
错在语域，coding 里用书面体僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Nails it: name one candidate, then sanity-check O(1).
Wrong — self-questioning loop, no progress.
Wrong — lists without choosing; no start.
Wrong register — written style stiff while coding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 哈希函数：把 key 映射成一个整数（索引）的函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash function maps a key to an integer index.

termDefinitions.meaning: O(1)（常数时间）：操作耗时不随数据量增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(1), or constant time, means the operation's cost doesn't grow with data size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 哈希集合：基于哈希、O(1) 判断元素是否存在的集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash set stores unique elements with O(1) membership checks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 链表：节点通过指针依次串联的线性结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A linked list is a linear structure where each node points to the next.

scenario: IKEA 的 ML 面试，面试官问：「Tell me about a production issue you debugged.」你有例子但要一秒挑，别像上次「Okay, um, okay, so」堆语气词。
scenario_en: In IKEA's ML interview the interviewer asks, "Tell me about a production issue you debugged." You have examples but need a beat to pick — not another "Okay, um, okay, so."
q: 想用一秒挑好例子，开口第一句怎么说？
q_en: You need a second to pick the right example — what's your opening line?
options: Okay, um, okay, so, one production issue that I personally debugged was, um...
Oh there were quite a few — config drifts, deploys break, alerts fire — so many stories I could pick, let me think about which is best to tell you...
Let me think for a sec, then I'll walk you through one I actually owned.
Permit me a brief moment to recollect a suitable production incident to recount.
tradeoff: 一句缓冲 vs 语气词填空：一句缓冲显得从容并预告结构；堆语气词只是把停顿念出声。
why: 讲故事前用「Let me think for a sec, then I'll walk you through one」买一个从容缓冲，好过用一串语气词把空白念出声。
why_en: Before a story, say "let me think for a sec, then I'll walk you through one" — a clean buffer beats stacking "okay, um, okay, so."
whenOtherWins: 只有当例子脱口而出、不用挑时，才直接开讲，省掉「让我想一秒」更利落。
options_en: Okay, um, okay, so, one production issue that I personally debugged was, um...
Oh there were quite a few — config drifts, deploys break, alerts fire — so many stories I could pick, let me think about which is best to tell you...
Let me think for a sec, then I'll walk you through one I actually owned.
Permit me a brief moment to recollect a suitable production incident to recount.
optionMeanings: 连堆「okay, um, okay, so」把停顿念出声。
罗列一堆故障类型，迟迟不挑一个讲。
一句「让我想一秒，再讲一个」买缓冲并预告结构。
用「Permit me a brief moment」的公文腔。
optionMeanings_en: Stacks 'okay, um, okay, so,' voicing the pause.
Lists failure types, never picks one to tell.
'Let me think a sec, then I'll walk you through one' — clean buffer.
Bureaucratic 'permit me a brief moment' register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 空白被念出声，显得慌。
铺垫太长，对方等不到故事。
停顿从容，对方知道故事马上来。
过度正式，像客服邮件。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The blank is spoken aloud — looks rattled.
Wind-up too long; no story arrives.
Composed pause; they know the story's coming.
Over-formal — like a support email.
optionDirectness: 错在语气词填空，等于把停顿念出声。
错在罗列不收口，迟迟不进故事。
抓住「缓冲句 + 预告结构」的起手。
错在语域，口语用公文体僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — filler for a pause, a spoken blank.
Wrong — listing without landing on a story.
Nails it: a buffer line that previews the story.
Wrong register — bureaucratese is stiff aloud.

termDefinitions.meaning: 配置漂移：环境的实际配置与预期/代码里声明的配置逐渐不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Config drift is when a system's real configuration slowly diverges from its intended, declared state.

scenario: Alterion coding 轮拿到 Trie 题（前缀树，支持 insert 和 startsWith）。你不确定 startsWith 到底返回什么，别像上次「why do we want a list of string」自问自答。
scenario_en: In an Alterion coding round you get a Trie problem (prefix tree with insert and startsWith). You're unsure what startsWith returns — don't self-ask "why do we want a list of string" like last time.
q: 需求还没完全确认，动手前第一句该怎么说？
q_en: The ask is still fuzzy — what's your first line before coding?
options: Before I dive in, let me make sure I get the ask — startsWith returns all words with that prefix, right?
So start with... then we return a list of str, why do we want a list of string, let me, let me think...
Okay so there's insert, there's startsWith, return types, edge cases, empty prefix, no matches — so much to consider, let me talk through all of it...
Kindly permit me to confirm the precise specification of the startsWith operation prior to implementation.
tradeoff: 先确认需求 vs 边猜边写：先跟面试官对齐省得写错方向，代价是多花一次确认；自己猜可能整段返工。
why: 需求不清时先「Before I dive in, let me make sure I understand the requirement」把它确认成一句 yes/no，比自问自答「why do we want...」把困惑说给自己听强。
why_en: When the ask is fuzzy, say "before I dive in, let me make sure I get the requirement" and confirm it as a yes/no — don't mutter the confusion to yourself.
whenOtherWins: 只有当题目已经写得非常明确、没有歧义时，才不用再确认，直接开写更快。
options_en: Before I dive in, let me make sure I get the ask — startsWith returns all words with that prefix, right?
So start with... then we return a list of str, why do we want a list of string, let me, let me think...
Okay so there's insert, there's startsWith, return types, edge cases, empty prefix, no matches — so much to consider, let me talk through all of it...
Kindly permit me to confirm the precise specification of the startsWith operation prior to implementation.
optionMeanings: 先把需求确认成一句 yes/no，再动手。
自问「why a list of string」，边猜边卡。
罗列 insert/边界等一堆点，迟迟不确认核心需求。
用「Kindly permit me」的公文腔请求确认。
optionMeanings_en: Confirms the ask as a yes/no first, then starts.
Self-asks 'why a list of string,' guessing and stalling.
Lists insert/edge cases, never nails the core ask.
Asks to confirm in a stiff 'kindly permit me' register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 方向对齐，避免写错整段返工。
把困惑说给自己，显得没把握。
铺垫太长，还没确认就发散。
过度正式，像法律文书。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Aligns direction, avoids rewriting the whole thing.
Mutters confusion to self — reads as unsure.
Long wind-up; diverges before confirming.
Over-formal — like a legal document.
optionDirectness: 抓住「动手前把需求确认成 yes/no」。
错在自问自答，把困惑念出声。
错在发散罗列，没锁定核心需求。
错在语域，口语用公文体僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Nails it: confirm the requirement as a yes/no before coding.
Wrong — self-questioning voices the confusion.
Wrong — diverges without locking the core ask.
Wrong register — bureaucratese is stiff aloud.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前缀树（Trie）：按字符逐层存字符串、共享公共前缀的树结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trie is a tree that stores strings character by character, sharing common prefixes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前缀：一个字符串开头的若干字符。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A prefix is the leading characters at the start of a string.

scenario: Majestic 面试，面试官问：「Which data structure would you use to store that?」你想说哈希表，但上次开口成「So hash map, hash map, read read」原地打转。
scenario_en: In a Majestic interview the interviewer asks, "Which data structure would you use to store that?" You mean a hash map, but last time you looped "so hash map, hash map, read read."
q: 心里已有答案，怎么一句给出方向而不复读打转？
q_en: You already have the answer — how do you state a direction in one line without looping?
options: So hash map, hash map, read read, so if I want to store user info that I read and write a lot, then...
My first instinct is a hash map — let me say why that fits here.
Well it depends — could be a hash map, a tree, an array — each has pros and cons on reads, writes, memory, let me weigh those out loud...
I would elect to employ a hash map, the rationale for which I shall presently expound.
tradeoff: 一句定方向 vs 复读词卡住：先亮答案再解释显得果断；重复关键词只是把犹豫暴露出来。
why: 已有答案时用「My first instinct is X」一句给方向再解释，别把关键词复读成原地打转。
why_en: With an answer in mind, say "my first instinct is X, let me say why" — don't loop "hash map, hash map, read read" in place.
whenOtherWins: 只有当面试官明显想让你先对比几种结构时，才用「it depends」展开，而不是直接报一个。
options_en: So hash map, hash map, read read, so if I want to store user info that I read and write a lot, then...
My first instinct is a hash map — let me say why that fits here.
Well it depends — could be a hash map, a tree, an array — each has pros and cons on reads, writes, memory, let me weigh those out loud...
I would elect to employ a hash map, the rationale for which I shall presently expound.
optionMeanings: 复读「hash map, hash map, read read」原地打转。
先亮答案是哈希表，再解释为何合适。
说「it depends」罗列多种结构，不给答案。
用「I shall presently expound」的书面公文腔。
optionMeanings_en: Loops 'hash map, hash map, read read' in place.
'My first instinct is a hash map,' then explains the fit.
Says 'it depends,' lists structures, gives no answer.
Stiff 'I shall presently expound' register.
optionScenarioImpacts: 犹豫被暴露，显得没把握。
果断给方向，再补理由，显得有掌控。
该给答案时含糊，显得没主见。
像背稿，不像对话。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Hesitation exposed — reads as unsure.
Commits to a direction, then justifies — in control.
Vague when an answer's expected — reads as noncommittal.
Scripted, not conversational.
optionDirectness: 错在复读关键词，把犹豫暴露。
抓住「先亮答案、再给理由」的起手。
错在该定不定，用「it depends」回避。
错在语域，口语用书面体僵硬。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — looping a keyword exposes hesitation.
Nails it: state the answer, then give the reason.
Wrong — dodges with 'it depends' when a pick's due.
Wrong register — written style stiff aloud.

termDefinitions.meaning: 哈希表：用哈希函数把 key 映射到桶，实现平均 O(1) 读写的键值结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash map uses a hash function to map keys to buckets for average O(1) reads and writes.

scenario: IKEA 面试，面试官问：「How did you prevent recurrence?」你上次一开口就复读「Recurrence, prevent recurrence, and so to prevent the same issue...」。
scenario_en: In an IKEA interview the interviewer asks, "How did you prevent recurrence?" Last time you opened by echoing "recurrence, prevent recurrence, and so to prevent the same issue..."
q: 想争取一秒思考又不复读问题，怎么起手？
q_en: You want a beat to think without echoing the question — how do you open?
options: Recurrence... prevent recurrence, yeah, so, to prevent the same issue from happening again, um...
Oh good question — prevention's such a big topic, testing, monitoring, reviews, alerts, guardrails, so many layers, let me think which to highlight...
Good question — let me take a sec. The main thing I added was stronger validation.
In order to preclude a recurrence of the aforementioned issue, I implemented several measures.
tradeoff: 一句缓冲进正题 vs 复读关键词：缓冲句买来思考又不显空；复读问题词只是原地回声。
why: 想买时间别复读问题里的词，用「Good question — let me take a sec」买缓冲，再直接给主干答案。
why_en: To buy time, don't echo the question's words — say "good question, let me take a sec," then give the core answer.
whenOtherWins: 只有当答案立刻就位、不需要缓冲时，才直接说主干，省掉「让我想一秒」。
options_en: Recurrence... prevent recurrence, yeah, so, to prevent the same issue from happening again, um...
Oh good question — prevention's such a big topic, testing, monitoring, reviews, alerts, guardrails, so many layers, let me think which to highlight...
Good question — let me take a sec. The main thing I added was stronger validation.
In order to preclude a recurrence of the aforementioned issue, I implemented several measures.
optionMeanings: 复读「recurrence, prevent recurrence」原地回声。
罗列一堆预防手段，迟迟不落到自己做了什么。
一句缓冲后直接给主干：加了更强的校验。
用「preclude the aforementioned issue」的公文腔。
optionMeanings_en: Echoes 'recurrence, prevent recurrence' in place.
Lists prevention layers, never lands on what he did.
A buffer, then the core: 'I added stronger validation.'

termDefinitions.meaning: 校验：在处理前检查输入/变更是否合法，不合法就拦下。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Validation checks that input or a change is legal before it's processed, rejecting bad ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 护栏：预设的规则/限制，防止危险操作真正生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Guardrails are preset rules that block dangerous operations before they take effect.

scenario: WOP 支付工程面，面试官抛开放设计题：「Design a system to store onboarding step status.」你想直接冲，但上次「where do we store it, let me think」乱起手。
scenario_en: In a WOP payments engineering round the interviewer opens with a design prompt: "Design a system to store onboarding step status." You want to charge in, but last time you fumbled "where do we store it, let me think."
q: 拿到开放设计题，动手前第一句怎么起手最稳？
q_en: Given an open design prompt, what's the steadiest first line before diving in?
options: Oh, there's an enum, um, where do we store it, let me think, where we store, I was starting an entity...
Before I dive in, let me confirm the requirements and rough scale — is this per-user and real-time?
Okay so a system — storage, the API, the data model, consistency, scale — so many pieces, let me start thinking through all of them one by one...
Prior to commencing the design, I shall solicit clarification regarding the functional requirements.
tradeoff: 先澄清需求与量级 vs 直接冲实现：先对齐范围避免设计跑偏，代价是花一两句；直接冲容易在细节里迷路。
why: 开放设计题先「Before I dive in, let me confirm the requirements and scale」定好范围和量级再动手，别一上来陷进存储细节。
why_en: For an open design prompt, lock the requirements and scale first — "let me confirm the requirements and rough scale" beats jumping to "where do we store it."
whenOtherWins: 只有当需求和量级面试官已经讲得很清楚时，才跳过澄清直接进设计。
options_en: Oh, there's an enum, um, where do we store it, let me think, where we store, I was starting an entity...
Before I dive in, let me confirm the requirements and rough scale — is this per-user and real-time?
Okay so a system — storage, the API, the data model, consistency, scale — so many pieces, let me start thinking through all of them one by one...
Prior to commencing the design, I shall solicit clarification regarding the functional requirements.
optionMeanings: 纠结「where do we store」，边想边卡。
先确认需求和量级，再开始设计。
罗列 storage/API/一致性等模块，迟迟不动手。
用「I shall solicit clarification」的公文腔。
optionMeanings_en: Frets 'where do we store it,' thinking and stalling.
Confirms requirements and rough scale before designing.
Lists storage/API/consistency, never actually starts.
Bureaucratic 'I shall solicit clarification' register.

过度正式，像述职报告。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Dives into details first — looks unstructured.
Aligns scope first — reads as experienced.
Module dump; diverges before designing.
Over-formal — like a status report.

termDefinitions.meaning: 枚举（enum, enumeration）：取值被限定为一组固定命名常量的类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An enum (enumeration) is a type whose value is restricted to a fixed set of named constants.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实体：数据模型里对应一张表/一类对象的建模单元。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An entity is a modeling unit in a data model, typically mapping to one table or object type.
